**What you'll do**

1. Read what the Royer R-121 is.
2. Learn how it hears: pattern, proximity, off axis.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Look up famous uses.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **R-121** is a **ribbon** mic from Royer Labs: a 2.5-micron aluminium ribbon between magnets, **figure-8**, passive (Royer).
- **30-15,000 Hz ±3 dB**, **-47 dBV**, max SPL above **135 dB** (Royer): it takes a loud guitar amp.
- Ribbons are typically bidirectional (Wikipedia, "Ribbon microphone").

## How it hears

- Front and back hear equally, the sides almost nothing; the **back is inverted**: mixed with a front mic it can cancel. Use **A + B** on the compare page to hear it.
- Royer: the offset ribbon makes the **back brighter** close up (the amount here is the site's).
- Close up, a directional mic gains **bass**: the **proximity effect** (Wikipedia, "Proximity effect (audio)"). Slide the distance and watch the low end of the graph rise.
- The response graph is the maker's published chart **digitised approximately** (the charts are pictures; the points here follow their shape as remembered: unverified).

## The mic

The Royer R-121 drawn after photos (proportions approximate, no logos). Drag the blue mic in the room (or use the Distance slider; the wheel or Angle turns it), choose a source and a room, press **▶ Hear it**. Voice is generated (the band has no singer); snare and kick are the band's kit; the guitar is the site's amp model. Nobody has compared the sound with a real mic.

```{=html}
<div class="mic" data-mic="r121" data-src="guitar"></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Microphone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone). Polar patterns as first-order sums: the cardioid = omni + figure-8, the figure-8's negative rear signal cancelling; ribbons' symmetric front and rear pickup.

"R-121." *Royer Labs*, [royerlabs.com/r-121/](https://royerlabs.com/r-121/). Accessed 26 Nov. 2026. Figure-8 ribbon, passive; 30-15,000 Hz ±3 dB; -47 dBV; 300 ohm; max SPL >135 dB at 20 Hz; offset ribbon, back side brighter close up.

"Ribbon microphone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribbon_microphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribbon_microphone). Typically bidirectional; Blumlein pair.

**For students**

"Proximity effect (audio)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)). Bass rises close to a directional mic; caused by the ports; not a true omni, but not necessarily absent on a multipattern mic's summed omni.
:::
<!-- /works-cited -->
